root_causes.description: The checkout service exhibits a severe latency anomaly: p99 server-span latency is pinned at 10000ms while every downstream dependency it calls (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) responds in under 50ms. The slowness originates inside checkout itself — not from resource exhaustion (CPU ~0.005 cores, memory ~25MB, 0 restarts, no K8s events) and not from errors (error_rate=0, 0 error traces). Slow traces (20-26s user_checkout_multi / order-consumed) complete successfully, indicating an injected or pathological processing delay in the checkout code path.

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99_latency_ms=10000.000 (mean/p50/p95/p99/max all 10000.000) across full window; downstream deps: cart=9.8ms, payment=1.98ms, email=47.6ms, shipping=4.85ms, currency=1.98ms, product-catalog=48.9ms

20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=354735ms; top traces: 1bca1a849d24103a (order-consumed, 25976ms, ok), a71d28df64cefb64 (user_checkout_multi, 20039ms, ok), 73866e2626c7cb75 (user_checkout_multi, 26581ms, ok)
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout traces complete in < 1s with 0 errors

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.005, max=0.007 cores — flat, no spike
evidence.expected_baseline: rules out cpu_stress; no anomalous CPU consumption

evidence.observed_value: memory_usage mean=24923648 bytes (~24.9MB), max=25731072 bytes — flat, no growth
evidence.expected_baseline: rules out memory_stress; no memory pressure or leak
rules out pod_crash; no container restarts
rules out http_abort; requests succeed, just slowly

evidence.observed_value: no K8s events found for checkout pods
evidence.expected_baseline: no pod kills, OOM kills, or evictions expected

root_causes.description: Frontend p99 latency is also pinned at 10000ms, but this is downstream propagation: frontend calls checkout (per topology frontend → checkout), and checkout's 10s server-span latency dominates the frontend request path. All other frontend dependencies (recommendation, product-catalog, cart, shipping, currency, ad) are fast, so frontend itself is not the origin.

evidence.observed_value: frontend p99_latency_ms=10000.000 while its other dependencies: ad=1.98ms, recommendation=4.97ms, cart=9.8ms, currency=1.98ms, product-catalog=48.9ms, shipping=4.85ms

root_causes.description: Considered whether a downstream dependency of checkout was failing, but this is ruled out: all six checkout dependencies (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) show fast p99 (<50ms), zero error rate across the entire service sweep, and checkout traces complete with status ok. The latency is internal to checkout's own processing, not a failing dependency call.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 for all services in the sweep (mean/p50/p95/p99/max all 0.000)
evidence.expected_baseline: no service is returning errors; dependency failures ruled out

remediation_steps: Profile the checkout service code path for injected/artificial delays, blocking synchronous calls, lock contention, or unbounded waits — the 10s flat p99 with fast dependencies and no resource pressure strongly suggests a fixed delay or timeout-bound wait inside checkout request handling.
Check for recent deployments or feature-flag changes (flagd) affecting checkout and roll back the last change to checkout if the latency coincides with a release.

Inspect checkout's gRPC client configuration and connection pools to cart/payment/email/shipping/currency/product-catalog for misconfigured deadlines or serial (non-parallel) fan-out that adds cumulative delay.
Add a p99 latency SLO alert on checkout (e.g., p99 > 500ms for 2m) and a synthetic checkout canary to catch latency regressions before user impact.
Once fixed, verify frontend p99 recovers below 200ms since its 10s latency is purely propagated from checkout.
